summary: SCIM was first designed for provisioning user accounts. This Standards Track document adds schema extensions so SCIM can also provision devices. It covers several onboarding systems, including Wi-Fi Easy Connect, FIDO device onboarding vouchers, Bluetooth Low Energy passcodes, and MAC Authenticated Bypass.

eli5.summary: School keeps a list of students. This adds a list of gadgets too, so the school can record each one and how it should get connected.

questions: how to provision devices with scim
scim wi-fi easy connect fido onboarding
subtitle: Extends SCIM from provisioning people to provisioning devices, with schemas for BLE, Wi-Fi Easy Connect, FDO, MAB and Zigbee.

tldr.problem: Onboarding large numbers of devices is hard, and different manufacturers use different ways to bootstrap trust between a device and a network.
tldr.mechanism: It adds Device and EndpointApp resource types to SCIM, plus extension schemas for BLE, Wi-Fi Easy Connect (DPP), Ethernet MAB, FIDO Device Onboard, Zigbee and endpoint applications. A SCIM server inside the deployment receives device details and applies local policy.
tldr.outcome: A deployment can learn which devices to expect and how to connect them using one familiar provisioning protocol, with new onboarding methods added as registered extensions.

today: RFC 9944 is a Proposed Standard published in May 2026. According to the metadata it has not been obsoleted or updated. New device extensions must be registered with IANA as described in the RFC.

sections.title: Why SCIM for Devices
sections.content:
The System for Cross-domain Identity Management (SCIM, RFC 7643 and RFC 7644) defines a protocol and schema for provisioning users. RFC 9944 shows it can be extended to provision device credentials and other attributes into a network. SCIM supports bulk operations, which helps because devices are often bought in bulk.

The RFC gives its reasons for choosing SCIM over NETCONF or RESTCONF with YANG: those focus on configuration rather than provisioning, SCIM is designed with inter-domain provisioning in mind and runs over HTTP, it is familiar in enterprises, and its data model suits provisioning. End devices are not meant to be configured directly.

The RFC warns that the SCIM database is essentially equivalent to a network's Authentication, Authorization, and Accounting (AAA) database and should be managed that way.
sections.eli5: Schools already have a good system for keeping lists of students. Instead of inventing a new system, this reuses it to keep a list of gadgets.

sections.title: Who Talks to Whom
sections.content:
In normal SCIM, a large organization is the client and a service is the server. For devices the roles are reversed: the SCIM server sits inside the deployment and receives information about devices expected on its network. It applies local policy about whether and how a device connects.

The client may be a vendor authorized to add devices as part of a sale, or an app that administrators or employees use to add, remove or look up devices, such as a phone app that scans Wi-Fi Easy Connect QR codes.

For IP devices, the server passes the needed information to the AAA subsystem so the device is allowed to connect. For non-IP devices, the response may include a control endpoint, and an application-layer gateway (ALG) is used to reach the device.
sections.eli5: A visitor at the front desk (the app) tells the building (the server) which gadgets are coming. The building decides who gets in and how.

sections.title: Device and EndpointApp Schemas
sections.content:
A new resource type, Device, has a core schema identified by urn:ietf:params:scim:schemas:core:2.0:Device. Only one attribute is required: active, a boolean saying the device is intended to be operational. The others are displayName, mudUrl (a link to the Manufacturer Usage Description file, see RFC 8520) and the read-only groups. Devices and EndpointApps can be put in SCIM groups whose member type is set to Device or EndpointApp.

A second resource type, EndpointApp, represents client applications that control devices or receive data from them. Its applicationType is either deviceControl or telemetry. It authenticates either with a certificateInfo object (a rootCA and a subjectName) or with a generated clientToken of up to 500 characters. If the server returns neither, external authentication such as OAuth must be pre-arranged.
sections.eli5: Every gadget gets a small card with its name and an on/off flag. Apps that boss gadgets around, or listen to them, get their own cards with a way to prove who they are.

sections.title: Onboarding Extensions
sections.content:
Each way of onboarding a device is a separate extension schema attached to Device. All extensions must be registered with IANA, and none is required by default.

  • BLE: deviceMacAddress (required), isRandom, irk (write-only, never returned), mobility, versionSupport and pairingMethods. Pairing extensions exist for pairingNull, pairingJustWorks, pairingPassKey (a 6-digit key) and pairingOOB.
  • Wi-Fi Easy Connect (DPP): dppVersion, a write-only bootstrapKey, optional deviceMacAddress, serialNumber, bootstrappingMethod and classChannel.
  • Ethernet MAB: only deviceMacAddress. The RFC calls MAC Authenticated Bypass a (very) weak legacy method that is not likely to work with MAC address randomization.
  • FIDO Device Onboard: an fdoVoucher, a PEM-encoded voucher. The SCIM server MUST know how to process it or forward it to an owner process.
  • Zigbee: deviceEui64Address and versionSupport.
  • endpointAppsExt: links a device to its EndpointApp resources and carries the enterprise control and telemetry endpoint URLs, for non-IP devices that need a gateway.
sections.eli5: Different gadgets say hello in different ways, like a secret handshake, a barcode or a name tag. Each way has its own form to fill in.

sections.title: A BLE Device Example
sections.content:
The RFC's BLE example registers a device named "BLE Heart Monitor" that is active, supports BLE version 5.4, has a public MAC address, and pairs with a passkey. A device can also list several pairing methods, for instance both passkey and OOB.

An IP-based device would instead use an extension like DPP, and the server hands what it learns to the AAA system. Appendix C walks through FIDO Device Onboard, where the voucher carries an X.509 certificate chain that the SCIM server recovers and passes on, and an identity is added to AAA.
sections.eli5: To register a heart monitor you fill in its name, its hardware address and its secret pairing code. Then the building knows who it is when it shows up.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
Because provisioning lets devices onto a network, each SCIM client MUST be authenticated. The RFC walks through the operations. Creation: an authenticated attacker could add devices with known vulnerabilities or a bot-like IP device, so administrators should layer extra policy and follow least privilege. Deletion is only a signal of intent; the server decides whether to revoke access, and a delete should trigger a workflow under local policy.

Reads and updates should be limited to clients that created the objects or those they authorize, since attackers with update access could cut devices off networks. If BLE passkeys are provisioned, the network may be able to fully control the device, so devices needing more protection must support finer access control themselves. SCIM logs reveal which devices are on a network and SHOULD be encrypted on disk and in transit.
sections.eli5: The guest list is powerful, so only trusted people may edit it, and the list itself should be kept locked up.
